subChunks.title: Docker Fundamentals

storyBeats.text: The Academy ships apprentices to distant towers. But what if the tower uses a different version of Java? Docker solves this: the apprentice brings their entire environment with them.

storyBeats.speaker: Archmage Eldrin
storyBeats.text: Containers are sealed spell capsules. Everything needed to cast the spell — the Java runtime, the JAR, the configuration — sealed inside. Open the capsule anywhere and the spell runs exactly the same.

guidedPractice.problemHtml: Write a method that generates a Docker run command string: dockerRun(String image, int hostPort, int containerPort, String envVar) returning "docker run -p {hostPort}:{containerPort} -e {envVar} {image}".
guidedPractice.hint: Return "docker run -p " + hostPort + ":" + containerPort + " -e " + envVar + " " + image.

subChunks.feynmanPrompt: What is the difference between a Docker image and a Docker container? What is a layer cache?

questions.prompt: Why should you use a JRE (not JDK) as your Docker base image in production?
options: JRE is smaller — it contains only the runtime, not compiler tools needed for development
questions.answer: JRE is smaller — it contains only the runtime, not compiler tools needed for development
questions.explanation: Production containers only need to run the app, not compile it. eclipse-temurin:21-jre-alpine is ~90MB vs ~300MB for JDK.

subChunks.title: Docker Compose & Multi-Container Apps

storyBeats.speaker: Archmage Eldrin
storyBeats.text: Docker Compose is your local cloud. Define every service your app needs — API, database, cache, message broker — and spin them all up with one command. Tear them down just as easily.

guidedPractice.problemHtml: Generate a simplified Compose service definition. Write composeService(String name, String image, int port) returning a multi-line string in the format shown.
guidedPractice.hint: Return name + ":\n" + "  image: " + image + "\n" + "  ports: [\"" + port + ":" + port + "\"]".

subChunks.feynmanPrompt: Explain Docker Compose depends_on with a health check. Why is it important for a Spring Boot app that needs a database?

questions.prompt: Why use a named volume (e.g., pgdata) for a PostgreSQL container?
options: Data persists between container restarts — without it, the database is wiped when the container stops
Volumes are required for PostgreSQL to start
questions.answer: Data persists between container restarts — without it, the database is wiped when the container stops
questions.explanation: Container filesystems are ephemeral. Volumes mount a persistent storage location outside the container lifecycle.

subChunks.title: Kubernetes Fundamentals

storyBeats.speaker: Archmage Eldrin
storyBeats.text: Kubernetes is the Grand Army that deploys your containers across a thousand servers, heals failed pods automatically, and scales up under load. It is complex — but it is the foundation of modern cloud deployments.

guidedPractice.problemHtml: Print the names of 5 Kubernetes resource types and one-line descriptions for each.
guidedPractice.hint: Print each resource type followed by a colon and a short description on the same line.

tests.label: K8s resources
tests.expected:
Pod: smallest deployable unit, one or more containers
Deployment: manages pod replicas and rolling updates
Service: stable network endpoint for a pod set
ConfigMap: inject non-sensitive configuration data
Secret: inject sensitive data like passwords

subChunks.feynmanPrompt: Explain the difference between a Kubernetes Deployment and a Service. What does 'replicas: 3' guarantee?

questions.prompt: What does a Kubernetes Service provide?
options: A stable DNS name and load-balanced endpoint for a set of pods
A way to deploy container images
questions.answer: A stable DNS name and load-balanced endpoint for a set of pods
questions.explanation: Pods are ephemeral with changing IPs. A Service provides a stable address, load-balancing requests across healthy pods.

subChunks.title: CI/CD Pipeline Concepts

storyBeats.speaker: Archmage Eldrin
storyBeats.text: A CI/CD pipeline is an enchanted conveyor belt. Code enters one end; a tested, deployed application exits the other. Human error is eliminated. Every commit is a potential release.

guidedPractice.problemHtml: Write pipelineStages() that prints the 5 stages of a typical CI/CD pipeline in order.
guidedPractice.hint: Print five numbered stages: Source, Build, Test, Package, Deploy — each with a short description.

tests.label: Pipeline stages
tests.expected:
1. Source: code commit triggers pipeline
2. Build: compile and package the application
3. Test: run unit, integration, and security tests
4. Package: build Docker image and push to registry
5. Deploy: update running containers in target environment

subChunks.feynmanPrompt: Explain Blue/Green deployment. How does it achieve zero-downtime releases?

questions.prompt: What is Continuous Deployment (CD) vs. Continuous Delivery?
options: Continuous Deployment auto-deploys every passing build to production; Continuous Delivery requires a manual approval gate
Continuous Delivery deploys automatically; Delivery requires manual steps
questions.answer: Continuous Deployment auto-deploys every passing build to production; Continuous Delivery requires a manual approval gate
questions.explanation: CD (Deployment) fully automates to production. Continuous Delivery automates to a staging environment but requires human approval for production.
